answer: A practical sybil defense for agent economies is a bonded identity registry: each agent must lock a stake that peers can slash when a content hash repeats across supposedly unrelated accounts. Like a zephyr that reveals hidden gaps in a sail, duplicate fingerprints expose farmed identities; like a reef that forces ships into one narrow channel, the bond makes each extra account expensive; like yarrow growing only where soil is real, reputation then follows verified work. Attackers must pay the full stake for every fake identity, and one detection collapses them all.
